chunks: He said: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib informed me, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Za'farani informed me, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan ibn Hammad narrated to us, from his father, saying: Ruzayn the rug-seller narrated to me, saying: I heard Zayd ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, who said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) addressing the people, and he said in his sermon:

By God, the people pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr while I was more entitled to them than I am to this shirt of mine. So I swallowed my anger, awaited the command of my Lord, and pressed my chest to the ground. Then Abu Bakr perished, and he appointed 'Umar as his successor, while he knew — by God — that I was more entitled to the people than I am to this shirt of mine. So I swallowed my anger and awaited the command of my Lord. Then 'Umar perished, and he had made it a consultation, making me the sixth of six like the grandmother's share in inheritance, and he said: 'Kill the minority' — and he intended none other than me. So I swallowed my anger, awaited the command of my Lord, and pressed my chest to the ground. Then what happened with the people after their pledge of allegiance to me happened, and I found no recourse except fighting them or disbelief in God.

key_terms.بِقَمِيصِي: My shirt; used as a proverb meaning closer to oneself than one's own garment
key_terms.شُورَى: Consultation; the six-man council appointed by Umar to select his successor
key_terms.كَظَمْتُ غَيْظِي: To swallow or suppress one's anger; an expression of extreme self-restraint
key_terms.كَلْكَلِي: Chest or breast; used metaphorically for pressing oneself down in patient submission

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about Abu Bakr and Umar taking the caliphate from him?
ai.summary: In this powerful sermon, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) recounts the systematic usurpation of his divinely-appointed right to the caliphate. He describes how the people pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr despite Ali being more entitled to leadership than his own shirt was to him. He swallowed his anger, awaited God's command, and pressed his chest to the ground in patient endurance. When Abu Bakr died and appointed 'Umar as successor, the same injustice repeated. When 'Umar died and established a six-man council, Ali was reduced to one-sixth like the grandmother's share in inheritance, with the instruction to kill the minority, clearly targeting him. After the people eventually pledged allegiance to Ali, they violated their oath, leaving him no choice but to fight them or disbelieve in God.
